raw_response:
I will still run my 4.5 mu as a full wheat-maize rotation, because that is what fits my land, my labor, and my water. I have done this for many years, so I do not start from zero. I start from what has held yield in Quzhou County and then I adjust for cost and water. On a small farm like mine, every bag of fertilizer matters, but losing yield costs more than spending a little extra on inputs, so I will not cut fertilizer too hard. Since I have well irrigation, I will push wheat more steadily because wheat here responds clearly to water and nitrogen, and I will keep maize on a stable summer plan with hybrid seed, enough nitrogen, and two irrigations if rainfall does not carry it. For wheat, I will use improved seed, base phosphorus and potassium, and then split nitrogen between base fertilizer and topdressing at jointing. I will irrigate around overwintering recovery, jointing, and grain filling if the soil is short of moisture. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, give most phosphorus and potassium at planting, split nitrogen between sowing and the big bell-mouth stage, and irrigate around seedling establishment and tasseling if rain is short. I will keep pesticide use practical, not excessive: wheat mainly for weeds and one or two disease/insect passes, maize mainly for weeds and one insect pass if pressure shows. I will stay with rotary tillage because on 4.5 mu it is convenient, fast, and good enough for getting both crops planted on time.
